UserProfile.title: UserProfile
UserProfile.description: Represents a user profile in the Time application.

id.description: Unique identifier for the user profile.

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the user profile was created.

WorkGroup.title: WorkGroup
WorkGroup.description: Represents a workgroup in the Time application.

ownerId.description: Reference to UserProfile. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N WorkGroup) The user who created the group.

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the workgroup was created.

WorkGroupMembership.title: WorkGroupMembership
WorkGroupMembership.description: Represents the membership of a user in a workgroup.

id.description: Unique identifier for the workgroup membership.

workGroupId.description: Reference to WorkGroup. (Relationship: WorkGroup 1:N WorkGroupMembership) The workgroup the user is a member of.

userProfileId.description: Reference to UserProfile. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N WorkGroupMembership) The user who is a member of the group.

role.description: The role of the user in the workgroup (e.g., 'admin', 'member').

ServiceTask.title: ServiceTask
ServiceTask.description: Represents a service task within a workgroup.

id.description: Unique identifier for the service task.

workGroupId.description: Reference to WorkGroup. (Relationship: WorkGroup 1:N ServiceTask) The workgroup the task belongs to.

title.description: The title of the service task.

description.description: A description of the service task.

status.description: The status of the service task (e.g., 'production', 'finalized', 'pending').

assignedUserId.description: Reference to UserProfile. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N ServiceTask) The user assigned to the service task.

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the service task was created.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore data structure is designed to support a real-time service management application (Time), prioritizing secure and efficient data access. The structure emphasizes authorization independence and facilitates robust security rules.

**Authorization Independence:**

*   **WorkGroups:** The `WorkGroupMembership` subcollection denormalizes the relationship between users and workgroups. This eliminates the need for `get()` calls in security rules to determine group membership. Authorization checks can be performed directly on the `WorkGroupMembership` documents.
*   **ServiceTasks:** The `ServiceTask` documents include the `workGroupId`, enabling direct association with a workgroup.  No `get()` calls are required to validate a `ServiceTask`'s parent.

**QAPs (Rules are not Filters):**

*   The structure separates user profiles from workgroups and tasks.  This allows for distinct security rules for each entity type, preventing unintended data exposure.
*   Path-based ownership is used for user profiles (`/users/{userId}/profile`).

**Structure and Segregation:**

*   `/users/{userId}/profile`: Stores user profile information, accessible only to the user and potentially admins (if an admin role is implemented via a separate collection). This follows the Private Data access modeling pattern.
*   `/workgroups/{workgroupId}`: Stores workgroup information. The `ownerId` field indicates the group creator.  A subcollection `/workgroups/{workgroupId}/memberships/{membershipId}` manages user roles within the group (admin, member). This uses the Membership Map collaborative data access pattern.
*   `/workgroups/{workgroupId}/tasks/{taskId}`: Stores service tasks associated with a specific workgroup. Each task includes `assignedUserId` and `status`.  This segregates tasks by workgroup, simplifying security rules and enabling efficient querying.

This design enables secure `list` operations by ensuring that security rules can be applied directly to each collection without requiring complex filtering based on data content.
